messages.text: Good luck in this game! Before each move, ask yourself one thing: what does their last move threaten?
Their e5 put a pawn in the centre. Can they take anything of yours for free right now? What would you like your pieces to be doing in the opening?

Nothing of yours can be taken right now, and nothing of theirs hangs either. So look at your back row: your knight on b1, bishop on c1, bishop on f1 and knight on g1 haven't moved yet, and that is what is stopping you from castling.

messages.text: Good luck against Pip! Your one focus this game: before every move, look at their last move and ask what it is trying to do. Then check what they could capture after your move.
Their e5 put a pawn in the centre, and nothing of yours is in danger. Do you have any checks, captures or threats, and which pieces still need developing?
Their Nc6 protects the pawn on e5. Which two moves are you choosing between, and what could they capture after each one?
Their Bc5 now looks at your pawn on f2. Is that pawn safe, and what is guarding it?
Look at your pawn on f2: their bishop attacks it. Count the attackers and defenders there. What happens if they take it?
